summary: Join our training to master quantitative and qualitative research methods tailored for NGO programs. Equip yourself with skills to drive meaningful change.
lede: Research methods for NGO programs combine study design and evidence gathering to assess program impact. This course is for NGO program managers, monitoring and evaluation specialists, and research staff who need to evaluate outcomes and inform decisions. It covers sampling and statistical analysis, interviews and focus groups, and mixed-methods approaches for bringing measured results together with community perspectives.
audienceIntro: This course serves NGO professionals who must design, implement, and evaluate research studies that demonstrate program impact and inform strategic decisions.
audience: Policy Advocates using research findings to influence
modules: Research Foundations for NGO Program Impact
Statistical Analysis for Program Impact Assessment
Qualitative Research Methods and Data Collection
prerequisites: Participants should have basic experience with NGO programming and familiarity with monitoring and evaluation concepts. Previous exposure to data collection or analysis is helpful but not required. Access to a computer with internet connectivity for hands-on exercises is necessary.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
